# Introduction {#introduction}

![][image1]

**Last Updated:** 2026-05-20

## **Your own AI resume reviewer** {#your-own-ai-resume-reviewer}

Using Google AI Studio’s build feature, you can create any frontend application in React.js with a prompt. The Build feature in AI Studio generates applications that use the Gemini SDK and have no server-side components. The apps run in a sandboxed frame. For this workshop, you will create a tech resume reviewer that will score your resume out of 100 against a given job description. Let’s get started\!

## **What you’ll build** {#what-you’ll-build}

In this codelab, you'll build a resume reviewer that will score your resume against a job description:

* Your resume will be uploaded as text (not a file)  
* The job description will also be uploaded as text  
* The resume reviewer will give you a score (out of 100\)  
* It will also give you some actionable feedback in relevant sections and suggestions to change sentences.

![][image2]

| Note: You don’t need any coding experience, as the whole app will be vibe-coded (generated) by Gemini on Google AI Studio with a specific prompt. |
| :---- |

## **What you’ll learn** {#what-you’ll-learn}

* How to use Google AI Studio to build a “demo” app, with newly added features  
* How to deploy the app to Google Cloud Run  
* How to write an effective prompt on Google AI Studio (using Gemini) to create an app

This codelab is focused on Google AI Studio and a bit on Google Cloud Run.

---

# Prerequisites {#prerequisites}

Duration: 5:00

To begin, you will need to have the following pre-requisites sorted:

* A Google account   
* A web browser (like Chrome) to run Google AI Studio  
* A Google Cloud Platform project with some credit (GCP credits are provided; make sure you have applied the given credit, which is usually \$5)

# Google AI Studio \-\> Build {#google-ai-studio-->-build}

Duration: 1:30

## **Go to Google AI Studio** {#go-to-google-ai-studio}

To build a tech resume reviewer using Google AI Studio’s Build feature. You will first need to go to the Google AI Studio app. You can open the Google AI Studio app by visiting [https://aistudio.google.com](https://aistudio.google.com) in your favourite browser, or by visiting [ai.dev](https://ai.dev).

![][image3]

| Note: Google AI Studio is for personal use cases, whereas Vertex AI is for professional or enterprise use cases. Vertex AI now has Vertex AI Studio. |
| :---- |

### **Navigate to Build** {#navigate-to-build}

To go to the Build feature of Google AI Studio, you can click the Build menu item on the left navigation, as seen below:

![][image4]

| Note: You can try out other Gemini and Gemma models and their features on the “Playground” page, but that is not the scope of this workshop. |
| :---- |

In the next part, you will start writing your prompt.

# Prompt to app {#prompt-to-app}

Duration: 12:00

## **Use the correct model and framework** {#use-the-correct-model-and-framework}

Before using the prompt to create the resume-reviewer app, you will choose the right model and application framework. To do this, you will click the gear ⚙️icon on the top right corner of the Google AI Studio build page:

![][image5]

After that, select the “**Gemini 3 Flash Preview**” in the model and **React** as the framework, as seen below:

![][image6]

After that, close the settings and go back to the form to put in the prompt.

## **Input the intelligent resume reviewer prompt** {#input-the-intelligent-resume-reviewer-prompt}

As you want to build an intelligent tech resume reviewer, you will use the prompt given below:

The prompt

| Build an intelligent resume reviewer that analyses a resume against a job description, providing actionable feedback and suggestions based on the proven XYZ formula to help you stand out. Both the resume and the job description are also uploaded as text. Please take note of the following things when reviewing the resume: 1\. The primary purpose of the resume is to get the initial call or email from the tech recruiter, who is a non-technical person  2\. Please make the resume appeal equally to the engineering manager and other technical leaders who will take the interviews in later rounds.  3\. Keep yourself in the position of the resume receiver and frame the bullet points in a way to accentuate how the candidate can add value to the organisation Technically, please do the following:  1\. Please name the application "Resume Reviewer" and create it with an orange color theme. 2\. While uploading, show messages like "Parsing objective",  "Analysing job descriptions", "Creating a personalised review",  and similar messages. Please show the same message exactly once 3\. Show a percentage score of what the resume currently scores against 100, and things that can be improved in categories  like objective, job description, side projects, formatting, and use of language, etc 4\. Show detailed suggestions for each category nicely presented in a foldable bullet point list per category, highlighting the things to change per sentence. As a baseline, always use Australian English spellings for all the suggestions.  |
| :---- |

## **Prompt on Google AI Studio** {#prompt-on-google-ai-studio}

You can edit the prompt if you like, or just paste the prompt on Google AI Studio Build feature, then also find and click the “Add Gemini intelligence” option under the form, as seen below:

![][image7]

After that, click the Build button on the form. Then you will need to wait for the app to be built. It will take 2-3 minutes. The orange theme is mentioned in the prompt so that most of the generated apps look similar. 

 It will show something as follows when it is creating the app:

## **Resume reviewer app is generated** {#resume-reviewer-app-is-generated}

![][image8]

The full app is generated by Gemini over Google AI Studio. In the case above, it took just over 2 minutes to write the full resume-reviewer app in React.js.

# Use in preview mode {#use-in-preview-mode}

Duration: 3:00

You can check the code by clicking the **Code** option next to the **Preview** button.

## **Check the code (if you want)** {#check-the-code-(if-you-want)}

## **![][image9]**

If you look at the code, it is a React.js app. You can see the main logic of the resume review using Gemini LLM in the **/src/services/geminiService.ts**  file. It has generated its own prompt based on the prompt to generate the app.

To test the app, click **Preview** to return to preview mode. Then click the **full-screen** button to view the app in full-screen mode.

![][image10]

## **Test resume reviewer app in preview mode** {#test-resume-reviewer-app-in-preview-mode}

To test the generated app in full-screen mode, you will need a resume. For that, we will use a sample frontend engineer resume in text format. [Here](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/geshan/6218fdaac542c3314535dbe253c13341/raw/b3622236cb069753e4befc4093c21129baf62204/test-fe-resume.txt) is one for you to test; you can use your own.

As the sample Frontend engineer role, we will use this mid-level Frontend Engineer Role at Lorikeet AI in text format. [Here](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/geshan/6218fdaac542c3314535dbe253c13341/raw/b3622236cb069753e4befc4093c21129baf62204/z-fe-vacancy-text.txt) is the frontend engineer vacancy. It will look like the following:

![][image11]

After you click **Analyse Resume**, it will show the analysis step and take some time to show the result:

![][image12]

After the analysis is done, it will show the result, which would look something like:

As you scroll down, you will see more detailed analysis and suggestions as follows:

# Publish app {#publish-app}

Duration: 18:00

You can publish your app so you can share (boast about) it with your friends. For that, you will need a Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Project and some credits.

## **Create a GCP Project** {#create-a-gcp-project}

To deploy the resume reviewer, you can either use an existing Google Cloud Platform (GCP) project or create a new one. To create a new GCP project, navigate to the [create new project](https://console.cloud.google.com/projectcreate) page, then fill in the following details:

![][image15]

You can name it “resume-reviewer” and make sure to select the Billing account on which you applied the credit. Then click **Create**. 

It will inform you of the project being created:

![][image16]

## **Return to Google AI Studio** {#return-to-google-ai-studio}

After that, return to Google AI Studio and exit the app's full-screen preview. Then click the **Publish** option on the top right, besides the Share button, as seen below:

![][image17]

Then, click the **Get started** button as follows: 

![][image18]

## **Import the GCP project** {#import-the-gcp-project}

After that, import the resume-reviewer project you created in the previous step.

![][image19]

Then, select the project to use for publishing (deploying) the app as follows:

![][image20]

## **Set the API key**

In a new tab, go to Google AI Studio \- [https://ai.dev](https://ai.dev) ,

![][image21]

Then click on **Get API Key** on the left menu above Settings. After that, in the API keys page, click the **Create API Key** button on the top right:

![][image22]

Then select the project created in the previous step, **resume-reviewer,** and then click **Create key**.

The key will be created as follows:  
![][image23]

After that, go back to the tab where you started the publish app process.

## **Publish the app** {#publish-the-app}

On that page, go to the **Secrets** tab, click the select box beside **GEMINI\_API\_KEY**:

![][image24]

Then click **Select key** on the next pop-up, select the **Resume reviewer** project and the key you created in the last step:

![][image25]

After that, click Next,

![][image26]  
Then click **Select Key** 

![][image27]

After that, click **Apply Changes**. It will inform you that secrets have been saved. Close the notification as necessary.

Then, click **Publish** tab again:

![][image28]

You can also set the app's daily spending limit so it doesn't exceed your budget/credits. Click the pen button on the **spend cap** or set spend cap:

![][image29]  
If you have already set the spend cap, you can change it with the pen button:

![][image30]

## **Set daily spend limit** {#set-daily-spend-limit}

Then set the limit you want; in the example below, it is set at 25 cents a month, you can set it higher if you want:

![][image31]

Then click **Save**, as your app is already deployed or deploy it by pressing the **Publish App** button, you will see a URL which you can copy:

![][image32]

## **Use the app with a public URL** {#use-the-app-with-a-public-url}

Copy the app URL and paste it into a browser’s address bar, then hit enter to see your app working with a URL (not in preview mode):

![][image33]

You can share this URL with your friends and boast about the app you have created\!

---

# Congratulations {#congratulations}

Duration: 2:00

Congratulations, you've successfully built your own resume reviewer app and published it on Google Cloud Run\! The app can be used by anyone with the URL.
